question: I am a general-category student without a disability, applying fresh for the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (CSSS). I already have Aadhaar. List every document I need, including the documents needed to get them.
evidence: nsp-csss-faq Q19 lists for FRESH: 12th Mark Sheet and Family Income Certificate; Q6/Q23 require the Aadhaar-seeded bank account; Q14 has login with OTR.
note: Aadhaar is held, so its own enrolment documents are not expanded. Chain: OTR needs Aadhaar and face authentication (nsp-otr-faq Q5, Q16); seeding needs the bank account and the consent form (aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps); opening an account needs one OVD and PAN or Form 60 (rbi-kyc-md). Active mobile number linked with Aadhaar is also needed for OTR but has no vocabulary id.

question: I am an SC student without a disability applying fresh for the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students (CSSS). I have Aadhaar. What is every document I need, including documents needed to obtain them?
evidence: nsp-csss-faq Q19: FRESH needs 12th Mark Sheet, Family Income Certificate and Category/caste Certification for reserved category students.
note: Aadhaar is held, so its own enrolment documents are not expanded. Chain: OTR needs Aadhaar and face authentication (nsp-otr-faq Q5, Q16); seeding needs the bank account and the consent form (aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps); opening an account needs one OVD and PAN or Form 60 (rbi-kyc-md). evidence: nsp-csss-faq Q19: FRESH needs 12th Mark Sheet, Family Income Certificate and Disability Certificate (if applicable).

evidence: nsp-csss-faq Q19: RENEWAL needs only the Previous Year Mark Sheet; guidelines 4(v) say the income certificate is required only for fresh applicants.
note: Aadhaar is held, so its own enrolment documents are not expanded. Chain: OTR needs Aadhaar and face authentication (nsp-otr-faq Q5, Q16); seeding needs the bank account and the consent form (aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps); opening an account needs one OVD and PAN or Form 60 (rbi-kyc-md). question: An SC first-year student wants the Central Sector Scholarship of Top Class Education for SC Students and already has Aadhaar. List every document needed, including documents needed to obtain them.
evidence: nsp-topclass-sc-faq Q9: Valid SC Certificate, Income Certificate, Aadhaar, Aadhaar-seeded bank account, admission details, rank and fee details; Q17: an affidavit is required.
note: The income certificate must come from a revenue officer not below Tehsildar (or the employer for salaried parents), so it is kept as the generic income-certificate. Aadhaar is held, so its own enrolment documents are not expanded. Chain: OTR needs Aadhaar and face authentication (nsp-otr-faq Q5, Q16); seeding needs the bank account and the consent form (aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps); opening an account needs one OVD and PAN or Form 60 (rbi-kyc-md). question: A general-category girl admitted to the first year of an AICTE-approved degree course wants the AICTE Pragati Scholarship Scheme for Girl Students (Technical Degree). She has Aadhaar. List every document she needs, including documents needed to get them.
evidence: nsp-aicte-pragati-degree-faq Q22 lists SSC/10th, HSC/12th (degree level), Study/Bonafide Certificate, Annual Family Income Certificate and Parent Declaration; Q13 makes Aadhaar and an Aadhaar-seeded account mandatory.
note: The 10th and 12th pass certificates (as distinct from mark sheets) have no separate vocabulary id. Aadhaar is held, so its own enrolment documents are not expanded. Chain: OTR needs Aadhaar and face authentication (nsp-otr-faq Q5, Q16); seeding needs the bank account and the consent form (aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps); opening an account needs one OVD and PAN or Form 60 (rbi-kyc-md). Active mobile number linked with Aadhaar is also needed for OTR but has no vocabulary id.

evidence: nsp-aicte-pragati-degree-faq Q22 adds 'Category, if applicable' to the SSC, HSC, bonafide, income certificate and parent declaration list.
note: The 10th and 12th pass certificates (as distinct from mark sheets) have no separate vocabulary id. Aadhaar is held, so its own enrolment documents are not expanded. question: A student who already holds Aadhaar, an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, the 12th mark sheet and a family income certificate applies fresh (general category) for the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS). Which document should they apply for first?
evidence: nsp-otr-faq Q16: face authentication is mandatory for generation of OTR, so it comes before the OTR number.

question: A general-category student holding Aadhaar, an NSP OTR number (face authentication done), a bank savings account (not yet Aadhaar-seeded), the 12th mark sheet and a family income certificate applies fresh for CSSS. Which document should they apply for first?
evidence: nsp-csss-faq Q8: the student must submit the duly filled consent form at the bank branch, after which the branch seeds Aadhaar in the NPCI mapper.

question: A general-category student has Aadhaar, a PAN, an NSP OTR number (face authentication done), the 12th mark sheet and a family income certificate, but no bank account at all. They apply fresh for CSSS. Which document should they apply for first?
evidence: aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps: the customer visits the bank branch where he/she is holding an account to submit the consent form, so the account comes first; rbi-kyc-md: Aadhaar plus PAN satisfy KYC.

question: An SC first-year student holds Aadhaar, an NSP OTR number (face authentication done), an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, an SC certificate, an income certificate and admission/fee details. Applying for the Central Sector Scholarship of Top Class Education for SC Students, which document should they get first?
evidence: nsp-topclass-sc-faq Q17: benefits are restricted to two siblings and an affidavit is required; it is the only document still missing.

question: A girl in the first year of an AICTE-approved degree holds Aadhaar, an NSP OTR number (face authentication done), an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, her SSLC and 12th mark sheets, a bonafide certificate and an income certificate. Applying for the AICTE Pragati Scholarship (Technical Degree), which document should she get first?
evidence: nsp-aicte-pragati-degree-faq Q22 lists Parent Declaration (Appendix-III) among the documents to upload; it is the only one missing.

question: A second-year SC degree student (no disability, not admitted through counselling) in Karnataka holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, a Karnataka income certificate, an SSP student account, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents on SSP, an NSP OTR number (face authentication done) and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Applying for the SC Post Matric Scholarship (GoI), which document should they apply for first?
evidence: ssp-ka-home asks for the RD number of the caste/income certificate issued by the Revenue Department; ssp-elig-sc-pms limits the scheme to Scheduled Caste; ajsk-faqs says ID and address proof are mandatory for all certificates (held).

question: A second-year ST degree student (no disability, not admitted through counselling) holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, a Karnataka income certificate, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, but has no SSP account, no NSP OTR and no caste certificate yet. Applying for the Postmatric Scholarship for ST Students, which should they apply for first?
evidence: sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 32 gives the SC/ST caste certificate 21 working days, the only step with a legal time limit; SSP account and OTR/face authentication have no stated limit.
note: Assumes steps with no stated time limit do not outrank a known 21-working-day step. The SSP account and face authentication are also applicable now.

question: A second-year OBC degree student (Category 2A, i.e. a backward class other than Category-1; no disability) holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, an SSP student account, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, but no NSP OTR and no caste or income certificate. Applying for PostMatric for OBC Students Central / PM YASASVI, which should they apply for first?
evidence: tumkur-income-cert names Form F as the income and caste certificate for backward classes other than Category-1; sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 30 gives it 21 working days, while OTR and face authentication have no stated limit.
note: Assumes steps with no stated time limit do not outrank a known 21-working-day step.

question: A minority student holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a Karnataka income certificate, an SSP student account, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents and a bank savings account that is not Aadhaar-seeded. Applying for the Fee Reimbursement scheme for Minorities (Post-Matric), which document should they get first?
evidence: ssp-ka-home: Aadhaar seeding to bank account is mandatory for submission of application; aicte-aadhaar-seeding-steps: seeding starts with submitting the consent form at the branch.
note: OTR is not needed: ssp-ka-home asks for OTR only from SC, ST and OBC students.

question: An SC student holding only Aadhaar, ID and address proof and a voter ID applies for the SC Post Matric Scholarship (GoI). The deadline is 10 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 32: Caste Certificate (SC/ST) by the Tahsildar within 21 working days, which already exceeds 10.
note: ajsk-faqs says a certificate already in the e-Kshana database can be issued without waiting; the verdict uses the legal Sakala limit.

question: A second-year SC degree student (no disability, not admitted through counselling) holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, a Karnataka income certificate, an SSP account, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents, an NSP OTR (face authentication done) and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Only the caste certificate is missing. The SC Post Matric Scholarship (GoI) deadline is 30 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: Only the SC/ST caste certificate remains, and sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 32 gives it 21 working days, within 30.
note: Uses the SSP common application list in ssp-ka-home; Class 12 and previous-year result details do not apply to a second-year SC student.

question: An ST student holding Aadhaar, ID and address proof and a voter ID applies for the Postmatric Scholarship for ST Students. The deadline is 15 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 32: the SC/ST caste certificate takes up to 21 working days, more than 15.
note: ajsk-faqs says a certificate already in the e-Kshana database can be issued without waiting; the verdict uses the legal Sakala limit.

question: A second-year ST degree student (no disability, not admitted through counselling) holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, a Karnataka income certificate, an SSP account, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents, an NSP OTR (face authentication done) and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account; only the caste certificate is missing. The Postmatric Scholarship for ST Students deadline is 25 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: Only the SC/ST caste certificate remains; sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 32 sets 21 working days, within 25.

question: An ST student holds Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, an SSP account, the SSLC marks card, a university registration number, e-attested documents and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, but has no caste certificate, no income certificate and no NSP OTR. The Postmatric Scholarship for ST Students deadline is 30 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: The caste certificate (21 working days, Sakala) fits in 30, but the NSP OTR and face authentication have no stated time limit in any source.

question: An OBC student holding Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, an NSP OTR (face authentication done) and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, but no caste or income certificate, applies for PostMatric for OBC Students Central / PM YASASVI. The deadline is 10 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: ssp-ka-home requires the RD number of the applicable Revenue caste/income certificate, and sakala-compendium-en Revenue rows 10, 30, 31 and 33 give every such certificate 21 working days, more than 10.
note: ajsk-faqs says a certificate already in the e-Kshana database can be issued without waiting; the verdict uses the legal Sakala limit.

question: A backward-class student holding Aadhaar, ID and address proof, a voter ID, an NSP OTR (face authentication done) and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, but no caste or income certificate, applies for the BCWD Fee Reimbursement (Fee Concession). The deadline is 14 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: ssp-elig-bcwd-fee sets caste and income limits, ssp-ka-home asks for the Revenue certificate RD number, and Sakala gives each caste/income certificate 21 working days, more than 14.
note: ajsk-faqs says a certificate already in the e-Kshana database can be issued without waiting; the verdict uses the legal Sakala limit.

question: A backward-class student holding Aadhaar, ID and address proof and a voter ID, with no caste or income certificate, applies for the Vidyasiri Food and Accommodation Scheme (BCWD). The deadline is 10 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: Sakala Revenue rows 10 and 30-33: every caste or income certificate takes up to 21 working days, more than 10.
note: ajsk-faqs says a certificate already in the e-Kshana database can be issued without waiting; the verdict uses the legal Sakala limit.

question: A minority student holding Aadhaar and ID and address proof but no income certificate applies for the Fee Reimbursement scheme for Minorities (Post-Matric). The deadline is 20 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: ssp-elig-fee-minority sets an income limit, and sakala-compendium-en Revenue row 10 gives the Income Certificate 21 working days, more than 20.
note: 21 is a lower bound: tumkur-income-cert also asks minority applicants for a caste certificate, which has no vocabulary id for minorities. ajsk-faqs says a certificate already in the e-Kshana database can be issued without waiting; the verdict uses the legal Sakala limit.

question: A minority student holding Aadhaar, ID and address proof and an SSP account, but no income certificate and no Aadhaar-seeded bank account, applies for the Vidyasiri scheme for minorities. The deadline is 30 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: The income certificate's 21 working days (Sakala row 10) fit in 30, but bank account opening and Aadhaar seeding have no fixed legal limit (NPCI FAQ only says 'a couple of working days').

question: An OBC student holding only Aadhaar applies for the PM YASASVI Central Sector Scheme of Top Class Education in College. The deadline is 10 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: The guidelines ask for income and caste certificates, bank details and an affidavit without naming an issuing authority or time limit, and the NSP OTR has no stated time limit.

question: A general-category student holding Aadhaar, the 12th mark sheet and a family income certificate, but no NSP OTR and no bank account, applies fresh for the PM-USP Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship (CSSS). The deadline is 5 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: No source gives a legal time limit for OTR/face authentication, bank account opening or Aadhaar seeding.

question: An SC first-year student holding Aadhaar, an Aadhaar-seeded bank account, an SC certificate, an income certificate, admission details and the sibling affidavit, but no NSP OTR, applies for the Central Sector Scholarship of Top Class Education for SC Students. The deadline is 3 working days away. Can they make it?
evidence: Only the OTR and its face authentication remain, and nsp-otr-faq gives no time limit for either.
